value.hook: Open before typing any slash command into a Claude pane from pij (e.g. /model), or writing a tokio paused-clock test that builds Services
value.title: Driving Claude Code in-session: /model writes settings.json; tests on a paused clock

sections.name: body
sections.value:
Measured on Claude Code 2.1.321 (plan 225b, #215):
- In-session `/model <id>` rewrites the user's default "model" in ~/.claude/settings.json (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) every time. Snapshot the file's BYTES first (and whether it exists) and write them back; reserialising the JSON is not byte-identical, and a failed snapshot must refuse before switching.
- `/model` typed during a running `/compact` opens a "Switch model?" dialog at once. Confirming it (Enter) applies the switch immediately, and the compaction finishes undisturbed (190k to 13.7k tokens in about 19 s either way). With an empty context there is no dialog. pij presses only the dialog it opened (TmuxPort::press_enter), matched by its title and its "1. Yes, switch to" line.
- The proof the switch applied: settings.json took the new model id. A missed or late dialog leaves it unchanged; report that, never record the model.
Testing: tokio `start_paused` or `time::pause()` before `build_services` times out the SQLite pool ("pool timed out"), and on a paused clock a SQLite write reads as an idle runtime, so time jumps. Build services on the real clock, swap in FakeRegistry and an EventBus over FakeSpine, then call `tokio::time::pause()` inside the test.
A throwaway Claude probe seat: `pij-rs spawn --harness claude --role worker --cwd <wt>`, then `tmux send-keys -l` and Enter; afterwards `pij close`, `tmux kill-pane`, and check the pid is gone.
